Green-roof diagnostics: three roof types (Wien)

Source: vignettes/diagnose_green_roofs.Rmd
diagnose_green_roofs.Rmd

After the swale-trench (Mulden-Rigolen) optimisation, the results are to be validated against three roof variants feeding the swale: conventional roof (the status quo), extensive green roof and intensive green roof. The green-roof parameterisation was derived by Daniel Wicke (KWB) from SWMM-UrbanEVA (Hoernschemeyer et al.), v2 of 2026-10-13, and the engine behaviour was clarified with tandler.com (mails of 2026-10-08 and 2026-10-09):

  • The per-element switch Infiltration_aktiv controls whether pond water enters the element’s soil layers at all; the green roofs need 1 (the status-quo roof has 0, which is one of two independent reasons its ET is exactly 0 despite Evapotranspiration_aktiv = 1).
  • Endversickerungsrate is the separate exfiltration into the ground below; a roof is sealed, so the green roofs set it to 0 (the base.h5 value of 36 mm/h would silently drain the substrate out of the balance once infiltration is active).
  • Hoernschemeyer_aktiv exists only globally and gates the seasonal Growth/Shading modulation; referenced curves replace the static gfdoy/KSdoy values completely.
  • The roof-side Verschaltung taps the surface pond (von_Layer = 0), so substrate water leaves a green roof only via evapotranspiration; surplus ponds and drains to the swale.

The recipe itself lives in roof_type_values(), the monthly growth factors in default_growth_factors() / make_growth_curve(); the production workflows apply exactly the same functions.

This vignette runs a nine-scenario grid that validates the recipe and settles the points that could not be confirmed remotely (engine runs on Windows only):

  1. Recipe plausibility — conventional roof: ET share ~ 0 % and ~ 100 % discharge via the Verschaltung (for the legacy and the Hoernschemeyer frame alike); green roofs: ET share clearly > 0, intensive > extensive.
  2. Is the growth curve evaluated at all? — run 1 (2026-10-13) delivered identical roof ET for seasonal, flat and a 1.35→0.68 two-point curve (within 0.1 %-points) although the written inputs were verified correct. ext_growthlow (Growth_1 flat at 0.05) separates “curve ignored” from “supply limitation compensates the modulation”: if the curve is read, the roof ET must collapse.
  3. Named extra curves — tandler.com confirmed the curve set is an extensible named map, but could not say whether our engine build already supports it. Scenario ext_namedcurve writes a new //Kurven/Growth_Dach (flat 0.05) and points only the roof at it.
  4. Step interpolation — the time axis (hours since simulation start) is verified; the step semantics (“value holds until the next support point”) are checked with a two-point curve 1.0 → 0.01 (ext_stepprobe): under step interpolation the roof ET stays at the flat level, under linear interpolation it drops well below it.

A fifth observation rides along: in the May sweep the Dach water balance lacked WB_Evapotranspiration exactly in the combination Hoernschemeyer_aktiv = 1 + Infiltration_aktiv = 0; tandler.com sees no engine-side mechanism for that. With infiltration now active the variable should be present everywhere — the results table shows it.

Scenario grid

Geometry is fixed at Daniel’s reference design (the values are set explicitly in the run_one() chunk below); keineVerdunstungBeiRegen stays 0 on tandler.com’s recommendation (evaporation does occur during rain, and the effect is small).

param_grid <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario_name,   ~roof_type,     ~hoernschemeyer, ~growth,      ~purpose,
  "conv_legacy",    "conventional", 0L,              "flat",
  "status-quo anchor (legacy ET path, bit-compatible with published runs)",
  "conv",           "conventional", 1L,              "seasonal",
  "conventional roof in the new comparison frame (swale gets seasonal curve)",
  "ext",            "extensive",    1L,              "seasonal",
  "extensive green roof, shared seasonal Growth_1 (roof + swale)",
  "int",            "intensive",    1L,              "seasonal",
  "intensive green roof, shared seasonal Growth_1 (roof + swale)",
  "ext_flat",       "extensive",    1L,              "flat",
  "extensive green roof without seasonal modulation (reference for checks 2-4)",
  "ext_growthlow",  "extensive",    1L,              "growthlow",
  "check 2: Growth_1 flat at 0.05 -- if the curve is evaluated at all, roof ET must collapse",
  "ext_namedcurve", "extensive",    1L,              "namedcurve",
  "check 3: new named curve Growth_Dach flat at 0.05 for the roof, Growth_1 stays flat 1.0",
  "ext_stepprobe",  "extensive",    1L,              "stepprobe",
  "check 4: two-point Growth_1 (1.0 at start, 0.01 at end) -- step keeps ET at the flat level, linear halves it",
  "ext_komplett",   "extensive",    1L,              "seasonal",
  "like ext, but Ausgabemodus 'komplett' (historic mode name from workflow_eisenstadt-2005.Rmd) -- should make the engine write the ET-component time series"
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    ausgabemodus = dplyr::if_else(.data$scenario_name == "ext_komplett",
                                  "komplett", "Optimierung"),
    connected_area               = 1000,
    mulde_area                   = 75,
    mulde_height                 = 200,
    filter_hydraulicconductivity = 36,
    filter_height                = 300,
    storage_height               = 500,
    bottom_hydraulicconductivity = 12,
    rain_factor                  = 1
  )

DT::datatable(
  param_grid,
  options = list(pageLength = 9, autoWidth = TRUE),
  caption = "Nine scenarios: three roof types plus the growth-curve and output-mode diagnostics."
)

Input data 

path_list <- list(
  modelname = "Wien",
  root_path = file.path(tempdir(), "raindrop_green_roofs"),
  dir_input  = "<root_path>/models/<modelname>/input",
  dir_output = "<root_path>/models/<modelname>/output",
  dir_target_output = "<dir_output>/<dir_target>",
  file_errors_hdf5 = "Fehlerprotokoll.h5",
  file_results_hdf5_element = "Mulde_Rigole.h5",
  file_results_hdf5_flaeche = "Dach.h5",
  file_results_hdf5_verschaltungen = "<dir_target>_Verschaltungen.h5",
  file_results_txt = "Mulde_Rigole_RAINDROP.txt",
  file_results_txt_multilayer = "Mulde_Rigole_RAINDROP_multi_layer.txt",
  file_target = "<dir_target>.h5",
  path_base = system.file("extdata/models/wien/base.h5", package = "kwb.raindrop"),
  path_exe  = if (is_windows) kwb.raindrop::download_engine() else NA_character_,
  path_et   = system.file("extdata/models/wien/et.csv", package = "kwb.raindrop"),
  path_rain = system.file("extdata/models/wien/rain.csv.gz", package = "kwb.raindrop"),
  path_errors_hdf5 = "<dir_target_output>/<file_errors_hdf5>",
  path_results_hdf5_element = "<dir_target_output>/<file_results_hdf5_element>",
  path_results_hdf5_flaeche = "<dir_target_output>/<file_results_hdf5_flaeche>",
  path_results_hdf5_verschaltungen = "<dir_target_output>/<file_results_hdf5_verschaltungen>",
  path_results_txt = "<dir_target_output>/<file_results_txt>",
  path_results_txt_multilayer = "<dir_target_output>/<file_results_txt_multilayer>",
  path_target_input = "<dir_input>/<file_target>"
)

psi_s_mm <- function(kf_mmh) (3.237 * (kf_mmh / 25.4)^(-0.328)) * 25.4

paths <- kwb.utils::resolve(path_list)

timeseries_et_raw <- readr::read_delim(paths$path_et, delim = ";", col_types = "cd") |>
  dplyr::mutate(date = lubridate::dmy(date))

# The ET0 series has its own hour-0 origin (its first date); with the
# shipped data it coincides with rain_origin, but the calendar mapping in
# the checks below must not silently assume that.
et_origin <- lubridate::as_datetime(min(timeseries_et_raw$date))

timeseries_et <- timeseries_et_raw |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = as.integer(difftime(date, min(date), units = "hours"))) |>
  dplyr::select(-date) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(value)) |>
  dplyr::relocate(time, .before = value)
timeseries_et$time[nrow(timeseries_et)] <- ceiling(timeseries_et$time[nrow(timeseries_et)])

timeseries_rain_raw <- readr::read_csv(paths$path_rain, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::rename(datetime = time, value = rr)

# Calendar timestamp of simulation hour 0: needed to place the monthly
# growth-curve support points on the engine's hour axis. Taken BEFORE the
# NA filter so the axis matches the published pipeline (which computes the
# hour axis over the unfiltered series) even if leading values are NA.
rain_origin <- min(timeseries_rain_raw$datetime)
if (abs(as.double(difftime(rain_origin, et_origin, units = "hours"))) > 0) {
  message("NOTE: rain and ET0 series start at different timestamps (",
          rain_origin, " vs ", et_origin, ") -- calendar mappings use each series' own origin.")
}

timeseries_rain <- timeseries_rain_raw |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(value)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = as.double(difftime(datetime, rain_origin, units = "secs")) / 3600) |>
  dplyr::select(-datetime, -station) |>
  dplyr::relocate(time, .before = value)
timeseries_rain$time[nrow(timeseries_rain)] <- ceiling(timeseries_rain$time[nrow(timeseries_rain)])

# Align ET / rain end-times to the longer of the two
if (max(timeseries_rain$time) > max(timeseries_et$time)) {
  timeseries_et <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    timeseries_et,
    tibble::tibble(time = max(timeseries_rain$time),
                   value = timeseries_et$value[nrow(timeseries_et)])
  )
}
if (max(timeseries_et$time) > max(timeseries_rain$time)) {
  timeseries_rain <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    timeseries_rain,
    tibble::tibble(time = max(timeseries_et$time),
                   value = timeseries_rain$value[nrow(timeseries_rain)])
  )
}

# Convert rain from mm to mm/h (per 10-min interval), ET0 from mm/day to
# mm/h -- the engine reads both curves as rates on the hour axis.
period <- c(diff(timeseries_rain$time), mean(diff(timeseries_rain$time)))
timeseries_rain$value <- timeseries_rain$value / period
period_et <- c(diff(timeseries_et$time), mean(diff(timeseries_et$time)))
timeseries_et$value <- timeseries_et$value / period_et

t_end <- max(timeseries_rain$time)
sim_period_yr <- (t_end - min(timeseries_rain$time)) / (24 * 365.25)
rain_mm_per_year <- sum(timeseries_rain$value * period) / sim_period_yr

flat_curve <- function(value = 1) data.frame(time = c(0, t_end), value = rep(value, 2))
seasonal_curve <- kwb.raindrop::make_growth_curve(rain_origin, t_end)
# Run 1 (2026-10-13) showed seasonal, flat and a 1.35->0.68 probe all land
# within 0.1 %-points of each other -- in a supply-limited regime the
# modulation can compensate in the annual total, so the probes now use
# extreme values that force a visible water-balance difference whenever
# the curve is evaluated at all.
stepprobe_curve <- data.frame(time = c(0, t_end), value = c(1, 0.01))

Run the nine scenarios 

run_one <- function(i, timestep_hours, debug = FALSE, ...) {
  param_grid_tmp <- param_grid[i, ]
  paths <- kwb.utils::resolve(path_list, dir_target = param_grid_tmp$scenario_name)

  fs::dir_create(paths$dir_input, recurse = TRUE)
  fs::dir_create(paths$dir_output, recurse = TRUE)
  fs::dir_create(paths$dir_target_output, recurse = TRUE)

  fs::file_copy(path = paths$path_base,
                new_path = paths$path_target_input,
                overwrite = TRUE)

  h5 <- hdf5r::H5File$new(paths$path_target_input, mode = "a")
  new_path <- stringr::str_c(normalizePath(fs::path_abs(paths$dir_target_output)), "\\")
  vals <- kwb.raindrop::h5_read_values(h5)

  vals$`//Berechnungsparameter/Ergebnispfad` <- new_path
  vals$`//Berechnungsparameter/Zeitschritt_Infiltration` <- timestep_hours
  vals$`//Berechnungsparameter/Zeitschritt_ET` <- timestep_hours
  vals$`//Berechnungsparameter/Zeitschritt_Verschaltungen` <- timestep_hours
  vals$`//Berechnungsparameter/R-Plots` <- 0
  # "Optimierung" = lean outputs; "komplett" = full outputs incl. the
  # ET-component time series (mode name recovered from a comment in the
  # git history of workflow_eisenstadt-2005.Rmd).
  vals$`//Berechnungsparameter/Ausgabemodus` <- param_grid_tmp$ausgabemodus
  vals$`//Berechnungsparameter/Evapotranspiration_aktiv` <- 1
  # Tandler recommendation (2026-10-08, answer 8): evaporation does occur
  # during rain; effect is small, keep it active.
  vals$`//Berechnungsparameter/keineVerdunstungBeiRegen` <- 0

  # Daniel's reference geometry
  vals$`//Massnahmenelemente/Dach/Berechnungsparameter/Evapotranspiration_aktiv` <- 1
  vals$`//Massnahmenelemente/Dach/Allgemein/Flaeche` <- param_grid_tmp$connected_area
  vals$`//Massnahmenelemente/Mulde_Rigole/Berechnungsparameter/Evapotranspiration_aktiv` <- 1
  vals$`//Massnahmenelemente/Mulde_Rigole/Allgemein/Regen-Skalierungsfaktor` <- param_grid_tmp$rain_factor
  vals$`//Massnahmenelemente/Mulde_Rigole/Allgemein/Flaeche` <- param_grid_tmp$mulde_area
  vals$`//Massnahmenelemente/Mulde_Rigole/Eigenschaften_Oberflaeche/Ueberlaufhoehe` <- param_grid_tmp$mulde_height
  vals$`//Massnahmenelemente/Mulde_Rigole/Bodenschichtung/Startwerte_theta_ActualSoilMoisture` <- c(0.3, 0)
  vals$`//Massnahmenelemente/Mulde_Rigole/Bodenschichtung/Schichtdicken` <- c(
    param_grid_tmp$filter_height, param_grid_tmp$storage_height
  )
  vals$`//Massnahmenelemente/Mulde_Rigole/Allgemein/Endversickerungsrate` <-
    param_grid_tmp$bottom_hydraulicconductivity
  vals$`//Bodenarten/Bodenfilter/Ks_HydraulicConductivity` <- param_grid_tmp$filter_hydraulicconductivity
  vals$`//Bodenarten/Bodenfilter/Psi_Saugspannung_CapillarySuction` <-
    psi_s_mm(param_grid_tmp$filter_hydraulicconductivity)

  # Roof-type recipe (substrate, water path, vegetation + global
  # Hoernschemeyer frame) -- the same call the production workflows use.
  vals <- utils::modifyList(vals, kwb.raindrop::roof_type_values(
    roof_type = param_grid_tmp$roof_type,
    hoernschemeyer_aktiv = param_grid_tmp$hoernschemeyer
  ))

  # Curves
  vals$`//Kurven/ET0` <- timeseries_et
  vals$`//Kurven/Regen` <- timeseries_rain
  vals$`//Kurven/Shading_1` <- flat_curve()
  vals$`//Kurven/Growth_1` <- switch(
    param_grid_tmp$growth,
    flat       = flat_curve(),
    seasonal   = seasonal_curve,
    growthlow  = flat_curve(0.05),
    namedcurve = flat_curve(),     # swale stays unmodulated ...
    stepprobe  = stepprobe_curve
  )
  if (param_grid_tmp$growth == "namedcurve") {
    # ... and only the roof points at a NEW named curve with an extreme
    # value: if the build reads the named map, the roof ET collapses like
    # in ext_growthlow; if it silently falls back, it stays at ext_flat.
    vals$`//Kurven/Growth_Dach` <- flat_curve(0.05)
    vals$`//Massnahmenelemente/Dach/Parameter_Evapotranspiration/Kurve_gfdoy` <- "Growth_Dach"
  }

  tryCatch({
    # Creates //Kurven/Growth_Dach (and nothing else: all other datasets
    # already exist in base.h5) before the value write.
    kwb.raindrop::h5_ensure_datasets_from_values(h5, vals, strict = FALSE)
    kwb.raindrop::h5_write_values(h5, vals, resize = TRUE, strict = FALSE,
                                  scalar_strategy = "first", verbose = FALSE)
    if (h5$is_valid) h5$close_all()
    kwb.raindrop::run_model(path_exe = paths$path_exe,
                            path_input = paths$path_target_input,
                            debug = debug)
  }, error = function(e) {
    if (h5$is_valid) try(h5$close_all(), silent = TRUE)
    message(sprintf("[%s] run failed: %s",
                    param_grid_tmp$scenario_name, conditionMessage(e)))
  })
  invisible(NULL)
}

kwb.raindrop::run_scenarios(
  indices = seq_len(nrow(param_grid)),
  run_one_scenario = run_one,
  timestep_hours = 0.1,
  debug = FALSE,
  parallel = FALSE,
  show_progress = FALSE
)

Check 1 — recipe plausibility 

verdict <- function(ok, text) {
  message(sprintf("[%s] %s", ifelse(is.na(ok), "????", ifelse(ok, "PASS", "FAIL")), text))
  invisible(ok)
}

wb <- results |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    scenario_name,
    roof_type,
    dach_et      = .data$`connectedarea.WB_Evapotranspiration_`,
    dach_versch  = .data$`connectedarea.WB_Oberflaechenablauf_Verschaltungen_`,
    mulde_et     = .data$`element.WB_Evapotranspiration_`,
    dach_et_mm_a = round(.data$`connectedarea.WB_Evapotranspiration_` / 100 * rain_mm_per_year, 1)
  )
print(wb)
#> # A tibble: 9 × 6
#>   scenario_name  roof_type    dach_et dach_versch mulde_et dach_et_mm_a
#>   <chr>          <chr>          <dbl>       <dbl>    <dbl>        <dbl>
#> 1 conv_legacy    conventional     0        100        9.4            0 
#> 2 conv           conventional   NaN        100        9.24         NaN 
#> 3 ext            extensive       79.6       19.1     24.3          516.
#> 4 int            intensive       94.2        5.15    50.9          610.
#> 5 ext_flat       extensive       79.6       19.1     24.3          515.
#> 6 ext_growthlow  extensive       79.4       19.2     23.8          514.
#> 7 ext_namedcurve extensive       79.4       19.2     24.2          514.
#> 8 ext_stepprobe  extensive       79.6       19.1     24.3          515.
#> 9 ext_komplett   extensive       79.6       19.1     24.3          516.

g <- function(s, col) wb[[col]][wb$scenario_name == s]

# The Hoernschemeyer path reports the empty roof ET balance as NaN (the
# variable is written, its value is 0/0); together with ~100 % discharge
# via the Verschaltung that still is the sealed roof.
sealed <- function(s) {
  et <- g(s, "dach_et"); v <- g(s, "dach_versch")
  (!is.na(et) && et < 0.5) || (is.na(et) && !is.na(v) && v > 99.5)
}
verdict(sealed("conv_legacy") && sealed("conv"),
        "conventional roof: sealed in both frames (ET ~0 %, or NaN with ~100 % Verschaltung)")
#> [PASS] conventional roof: sealed in both frames (ET ~0 %, or NaN with ~100 % Verschaltung)
verdict(g("conv", "dach_versch") > 99,
        "conventional roof: ~100 % discharge via Verschaltung")
#> [PASS] conventional roof: ~100 % discharge via Verschaltung
verdict(g("ext", "dach_et") > 5,
        sprintf("extensive roof evaporates substantially (%.1f %% of roof rain = %.0f mm/a)",
                g("ext", "dach_et"), g("ext", "dach_et_mm_a")))
#> [PASS] extensive roof evaporates substantially (79.6 % of roof rain = 516 mm/a)
verdict(g("int", "dach_et") > g("ext", "dach_et"),
        "intensive > extensive roof ET (thicker substrate + higher KC/LAI)")
#> [PASS] intensive > extensive roof ET (thicker substrate + higher KC/LAI)
message(sprintf(
  "[INFO] seasonal-curve effect on extensive roof ET: %.1f (seasonal) vs %.1f (flat) %%-points",
  g("ext", "dach_et"), g("ext_flat", "dach_et")))
#> [INFO] seasonal-curve effect on extensive roof ET: 79.6 (seasonal) vs 79.5 (flat) %-points

# Plausibility anchor: the SWMM-UrbanEVA cross-check was run on
# 2026-11-10 and PASSED (setup review D. Wicke). Without surface
# ponding (berm height 0 mm -- the counterpart of the engine-side
# Verschaltung, which drains the surface pond without ponding), engine
# and UrbanEVA agree to at most 0.6 percentage points of roof ET
# (Wien 79.6/94.2 % engine vs 79.7/93.9 % UrbanEVA ext./int.;
# Bad Aussee 49.1/58.2 vs 49.7/57.8); the Wien extensive annual total
# ET is exactly 516 mm/a on both sides, and a berm-height series
# 0/0.1/1/2/5/30 mm shows monotonically rising ET (up to +17.6 pp).
# The modelled ~80 %/~94 % roof ET sits above typical literature
# retention for Central-European extensive green roofs (~45-60 %) but
# is reproduced by UrbanEVA under identical parameterisation -- the
# literature range describes the wet end of the climate gradient,
# which both models hit in Bad Aussee. Documentation:
# https://raindrop.kompetenz-wasser.io/optimisation/gruendach/urbaneva-gegencheck/
# Reference values below: UrbanEVA annual roof ET, Wien, berm 0 mm.
urbaneva_reference_et_mm_a <- c(extensive = 516, intensive = 608)
for (rt in names(urbaneva_reference_et_mm_a)) {
  mod <- g(c(extensive = "ext", intensive = "int")[[rt]], "dach_et_mm_a")
  ref <- urbaneva_reference_et_mm_a[[rt]]
  if (is.na(ref)) {
    message(sprintf(
      "[INFO] no SWMM-UrbanEVA reference ET yet for the %s roof (modelled: %.0f mm/a)",
      rt, mod))
  } else {
    verdict(abs(mod - ref) / ref < 0.25, sprintf(
      "%s roof ET within 25 %% of the UrbanEVA reference (modelled %.0f vs reference %.0f mm/a)",
      rt, mod, ref))
  }
}
#> [PASS] extensive roof ET within 25 % of the UrbanEVA reference (modelled 516 vs reference 516 mm/a)
#> [PASS] intensive roof ET within 25 % of the UrbanEVA reference (modelled 610 vs reference 608 mm/a)

Check 2 — is the growth curve evaluated at all?

Run 1 (2026-10-13) wrote verified-correct curves into the engine inputs (181-point seasonal Growth_1, Growth_Dach incl. reference, a 1.35→0.68 probe) and the roof ET still matched the flat reference to 0.1 %-points. In a supply-limited regime the seasonal factors (annual mean 1.0) can compensate in the annual total, so that result cannot distinguish “curve ignored” from “modulation washed out”. The ext_growthlow probe forces the distinction: Growth_1 flat at 0.05 caps the growth-modulated ET far below the water supply. Three outcomes: no shift at all — the curve is not evaluated (static gfdoy_GrowthFactor fallback, contradicting the Tandler answer of 2026-10-08); a small but deterministic shift (run 3, 2026-10-13: roof −0.2 pp, swale −0.5 pp) — the curve is read but the seasonal growth modulation barely shapes the annual balance, so the UrbanEVA monthly factors cannot shape the result (transpiration itself is large, ~370 mm/a per the ET decomposition below, supported by the passed UrbanEVA cross-check — why the gf modulation still washes out is an open mechanics question with tandler.com); a collapse — the curve works and the modulation matters.

# The engine is deterministic, so differences well below 1 %-point are
# real signal, not noise. Run 3 (2026-10-13) showed the growth factor
# 0.05 shifts the roof ET by only ~0.2 pp and the swale ET by ~0.5 pp:
# the curve IS read, but the seasonal modulation barely shapes the
# annual balance (transpiration itself is ~370 mm/a per the ET
# decomposition; the gf-insensitivity is an open mechanics question
# with tandler.com). Use both elements as sensors and a deterministic
# threshold.
et_flat    <- g("ext_flat", "dach_et")
et_low     <- g("ext_growthlow", "dach_et")
mulde_flat <- g("ext_flat", "mulde_et")
mulde_low  <- g("ext_growthlow", "mulde_et")
message(sprintf(
  "[INFO] Growth flat 1.0 vs flat 0.05: roof ET %.2f -> %.2f %% | swale ET %.2f -> %.2f %%",
  et_flat, et_low, mulde_flat, mulde_low))
#> [INFO] Growth flat 1.0 vs flat 0.05: roof ET 79.55 -> 79.35 % | swale ET 24.27 -> 23.81 %

d_dach  <- et_flat - et_low
d_mulde <- mulde_flat - mulde_low
curve_active <- if (anyNA(c(d_dach, d_mulde))) NA else
  (abs(d_dach) > 0.05 || abs(d_mulde) > 0.05)

if (is.na(curve_active)) {
  verdict(NA, "growth-curve check inconclusive (missing results)")
} else if (!curve_active) {
  verdict(FALSE, paste(
    "the growth curve has NO effect in this build -- the engine appears",
    "to use the static gfdoy value; escalate to tandler.com"))
} else if (d_dach < 5) {
  verdict(TRUE, sprintf(
    paste("the growth curve IS evaluated (deterministic shift: roof %.2f,",
          "swale %.2f pp), BUT even factor 0.05 barely moves the total --",
          "the seasonal growth modulation barely shapes the annual",
          "balance; the UrbanEVA monthly factors cannot shape the result.",
          "Transpiration itself is large (~370 mm/a per the ext_komplett",
          "decomposition, supported by the passed UrbanEVA cross-check);",
          "why the gf modulation washes out is an open mechanics question",
          "with tandler.com (query pending)"),
    d_dach, d_mulde))
} else {
  verdict(TRUE, "the growth curve is evaluated (extreme-low curve collapses the roof ET)")
}
#> [PASS] the growth curve IS evaluated (deterministic shift: roof 0.20, swale 0.46 pp), BUT even factor 0.05 barely moves the total -- the seasonal growth modulation barely shapes the annual balance; the UrbanEVA monthly factors cannot shape the result. Transpiration itself is large (~370 mm/a per the ext_komplett decomposition, supported by the passed UrbanEVA cross-check); why the gf modulation washes out is an open mechanics question with tandler.com (query pending)

Check 3 — does the engine read a new named curve?

ext_namedcurve points only the roof at a new curve //Kurven/Growth_Dach (flat 0.05) while Growth_1 stays flat 1.0. Decidable only if check 2 shows the curve is evaluated at all. The fingerprint of a working named-curve map is: roof ET equals ext_growthlow while the swale ET stays at the ext_flat level.

et_named    <- g("ext_namedcurve", "dach_et")
mulde_named <- g("ext_namedcurve", "mulde_et")
message(sprintf(
  "[INFO] namedcurve(0.05): roof ET %.2f %% (growthlow ref %.2f, flat ref %.2f) | swale ET %.2f %% (flat ref %.2f)",
  et_named, et_low, et_flat, mulde_named, mulde_flat))
#> [INFO] namedcurve(0.05): roof ET 79.35 % (growthlow ref 79.35, flat ref 79.55) | swale ET 24.24 % (flat ref 24.27)

if (isTRUE(curve_active) && !anyNA(c(et_named, mulde_named))) {
  roof_follows_curve <- abs(et_named - et_low) < abs(et_named - et_flat)
  swale_stays_flat   <- abs(mulde_named - mulde_flat) < abs(mulde_named - mulde_low)
  named_works <- roof_follows_curve && swale_stays_flat
  verdict(named_works, sprintf(
    "Growth_Dach %s by this engine build%s",
    ifelse(named_works, "is read and applies to the roof only (named curve map works)",
           "is NOT read as intended"),
    ifelse(named_works, "", sprintf(
      " (roof follows curve: %s, swale stays flat: %s)",
      roof_follows_curve, swale_stays_flat))))
} else {
  verdict(NA, "named-curve check inconclusive (requires check 2 = curve evaluated and results for ext_namedcurve)")
}
#> [PASS] Growth_Dach is read and applies to the roof only (named curve map works) by this engine build

Check 4 — step vs. linear curve interpolation

The ext_stepprobe curve has two support points: 1.0 at hour 0 and 0.01 at the series end. Under step interpolation the factor stays 1.0 for the whole run, so roof and swale ET match ext_flat exactly; under linear interpolation the factor averages ~0.5, which must show roughly half the (small but deterministic) ext_growthlow shift. Decidable only if check 2 shows the curve is evaluated.

et_step    <- g("ext_stepprobe", "dach_et")
mulde_step <- g("ext_stepprobe", "mulde_et")
message(sprintf(
  "[INFO] stepprobe: roof ET %.2f %% (flat ref %.2f, growthlow ref %.2f) | swale ET %.2f %% (flat ref %.2f, growthlow ref %.2f)",
  et_step, et_flat, et_low, mulde_step, mulde_flat, mulde_low))
#> [INFO] stepprobe: roof ET 79.55 % (flat ref 79.55, growthlow ref 79.35) | swale ET 24.27 % (flat ref 24.27, growthlow ref 23.81)

if (isTRUE(curve_active) && !anyNA(c(et_step, mulde_step))) {
  # Distance to the flat fingerprint vs. to the halfway (linear) point,
  # summed over both sensors.
  dist_flat <- abs(et_step - et_flat) + abs(mulde_step - mulde_flat)
  dist_lin  <- abs(et_step - (et_flat + et_low) / 2) +
    abs(mulde_step - (mulde_flat + mulde_low) / 2)
  if (dist_flat < dist_lin) {
    verdict(TRUE, sprintf(
      paste("interpolation is STEP (value holds to the next support point;",
            "distance to flat fingerprint %.3f vs linear %.3f) --",
            "make_growth_curve()'s month-start support points are correct"),
      dist_flat, dist_lin))
  } else {
    verdict(FALSE, sprintf(
      paste("interpolation looks LINEAR (distance to linear fingerprint %.3f",
            "vs flat %.3f) -- switch make_growth_curve() to month-midpoint",
            "support points"),
      dist_lin, dist_flat))
  }
} else {
  verdict(NA, "interpolation check inconclusive (requires check 2 = curve evaluated and results for ext_stepprobe)")
}
#> [PASS] interpolation is STEP (value holds to the next support point; distance to flat fingerprint 0.000 vs linear 0.330) -- make_growth_curve()'s month-start support points are correct

# ET-component deep-dive: the "Zusaetzliche Variablen Evapotranspiration"
# group of Dach.h5 is not written in Ausgabemodus "Optimierung" (checked
# empty on the 2026-10-13 run); the ext_komplett scenario runs the same
# extensive roof with Ausgabemodus "komplett", which should include it.
read_roof_et <- function(scenario) {
  p <- kwb.utils::resolve(path_list, dir_target = scenario)
  if (!file.exists(p$path_results_hdf5_flaeche)) return(NULL)
  h5 <- hdf5r::H5File$new(p$path_results_hdf5_flaeche, mode = "r")
  on.exit(try(h5$close_all(), silent = TRUE), add = TRUE)
  grp <- tryCatch(h5[["Zusaetzliche Variablen Evapotranspiration"]],
                  error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(grp)) return(NULL)
  out <- kwb.raindrop::read_hdf5_timeseries(grp)
  if (nrow(out) == 0L) return(NULL)
  out
}

# Sanity check first: the output mode must not change the physics.
message(sprintf(
  "[INFO] roof ET share ext (Optimierung) = %.1f %% vs ext_komplett = %.1f %% (should match)",
  g("ext", "dach_et"), g("ext_komplett", "dach_et")))
#> [INFO] roof ET share ext (Optimierung) = 79.6 % vs ext_komplett = 79.6 % (should match)

et_components <- read_roof_et("ext_komplett")
if (is.null(et_components)) {
  message(paste(
    "[INFO] no ET-component time series in Dach.h5 even with Ausgabemodus",
    "'komplett' -- mode name wrong or scenario failed; ask tandler.com"))
} else {
  message("[INFO] ET components available: ",
          paste(unique(et_components$variable), collapse = ", "))
  # Run 4 (2026-10-13) showed the group holds potential rates and state
  # variables, not the actual component fluxes of Gl. 15. Integrate only
  # the mm/h rates; state-like variables must not be summed over time.
  rate_vars <- c("ESp_es_PotentialSoilEvaporation",
                 "ETp_PotentialTranspiration",
                 "Pnet_PrecipRemainingAfterIntercep")
  comp_totals <- et_components |>
    dplyr::filter(.data$variable %in% rate_vars) |>
    dplyr::group_by(.data$variable) |>
    dplyr::arrange(.data$time, .by_group = TRUE) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      mm_total = sum(.data$value * c(diff(.data$time), mean(diff(.data$time)))),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(mm_per_year = round(.data$mm_total / sim_period_yr, 1))
  print(comp_totals)
  message("[INFO] state-like variables (not integrated): ",
          paste(setdiff(unique(et_components$variable), rate_vars), collapse = ", "))
  # Derived interception evaporation: gross roof rain minus the
  # post-interception net precipitation.
  pnet <- comp_totals$mm_per_year[
    comp_totals$variable == "Pnet_PrecipRemainingAfterIntercep"]
  if (length(pnet) == 1L) {
    message(sprintf(
      "[INFO] derived interception evaporation ~ %.0f mm/a (gross roof rain %.0f - Pnet %.0f)",
      rain_mm_per_year - pnet, rain_mm_per_year, pnet))
  }
}
#> [INFO] ET components available: Ab_WaterWettedLeafArea, ESa_DeltaTheta, ESp_es_PotentialSoilEvaporation, ETp_PotentialTranspiration, Pnet_PrecipRemainingAfterIntercep, Wrel_RelativeSoilMoisture, available_soil_water, es_EvapFactor
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>   variable                          mm_total mm_per_year
#>   <chr>                                <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1 ESp_es_PotentialSoilEvaporation      1560.        104 
#> 2 ETp_PotentialTranspiration           9082.        606.
#> 3 Pnet_PrecipRemainingAfterIntercep    9081.        606.
#> [INFO] state-like variables (not integrated): Ab_WaterWettedLeafArea, ESa_DeltaTheta, Wrel_RelativeSoilMoisture, available_soil_water, es_EvapFactor
#> [INFO] derived interception evaporation ~ 42 mm/a (gross roof rain 648 - Pnet 606)

# Engine error logs: totals per scenario plus a breakdown by error
# category (run 1: only benign "Hinweis" numerics entries, no complaint
# about the unknown curve name).
err <- suppressWarnings(kwb.raindrop::read_raindrop_errors(
  simulation_names = param_grid$scenario_name,
  path_list = path_list
))
print(dplyr::select(err, "scenario_name", "file_exists", "number_of_errors"))
#> # A tibble: 9 × 3
#>   scenario_name  file_exists number_of_errors
#>   <chr>          <lgl>                  <int>
#> 1 conv_legacy    TRUE                     183
#> 2 conv           TRUE                     188
#> 3 ext            TRUE                     247
#> 4 int            TRUE                     224
#> 5 ext_flat       TRUE                     260
#> 6 ext_growthlow  TRUE                     365
#> 7 ext_namedcurve TRUE                     385
#> 8 ext_stepprobe  TRUE                     262
#> 9 ext_komplett   TRUE                     247
# The engine writes its error texts in the Windows codepage (CP1252);
# the mis-tagged bytes crash the htmlwidgets JSON encoder ("input string
# 1 is invalid UTF-8"), so normalise them before the datatable.
to_utf8 <- function(x) {
  x <- as.character(x)
  bad <- !is.na(x) & !validUTF8(x)
  x[bad] <- iconv(x[bad], from = "CP1252", to = "UTF-8", sub = "byte")
  x
}
err_categories <- err |>
  dplyr::select("scenario_name", "errors") |>
  tidyr::unnest("errors") |>
  dplyr::mutate(Fehlerbeschreibung = to_utf8(.data$Fehlerbeschreibung)) |>
  dplyr::count(.data$scenario_name, .data$Fehlerbeschreibung, sort = TRUE)
DT::datatable(
  err_categories,
  options = list(pageLength = 10, autoWidth = TRUE),
  caption = "Engine error-log categories per scenario."
)

Check 5 — Dach WB_Evapotranspiration present? 

has_wb_et <- vapply(param_grid$scenario_name, function(s) {
  wb_names <- tryCatch(
    simulation_results[[s]]$connected_area$water_balance$variable,
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  any(grepl("WB_Evapotranspiration", c(wb_names,
    names(simulation_results[[s]]$connected_area$water_balance))))
}, logical(1))
print(tibble::tibble(scenario_name = param_grid$scenario_name, has_wb_et))

Persist the applied settings

The XLSX dump (base values, per-scenario diffs against base.h5, full per-scenario views) is the file to send to Daniel / tandler.com for review of what exactly each scenario changed.

format_h5_value <- function(v) {
  if (is.null(v)) {
    "<NULL>"
  } else if (is.data.frame(v)) {
    sprintf("[time series: %d rows; cols: %s]",
            nrow(v), paste(names(v), collapse = ", "))
  } else if (length(v) > 1L) {
    paste(format(v, trim = TRUE), collapse = ", ")
  } else {
    format(v, trim = TRUE)
  }
}

vals_to_tibble <- function(vals) {
  tibble::tibble(
    parameter = names(vals),
    value     = vapply(vals, format_h5_value, character(1L))
  ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(parameter)
}

vals_equal <- function(a, b) {
  if (is.null(a) || is.null(b)) return(identical(a, b))
  isTRUE(all.equal(a, b))
}

h5_base <- hdf5r::H5File$new(path_base, mode = "r")
base_vals <- kwb.raindrop::h5_read_values(h5_base)
h5_base$close_all()

sheets <- list(base = vals_to_tibble(base_vals))
applied_rows <- list()
for (sname in param_grid$scenario_name) {
  p <- kwb.utils::resolve(path_list, dir_target = sname)
  h5_s <- hdf5r::H5File$new(p$path_target_input, mode = "r")
  scenario_vals <- kwb.raindrop::h5_read_values(h5_s)
  h5_s$close_all()
  sheets[[sname]] <- vals_to_tibble(scenario_vals)
  for (k in union(names(base_vals), names(scenario_vals))) {
    if (!vals_equal(base_vals[[k]], scenario_vals[[k]])) {
      applied_rows[[length(applied_rows) + 1L]] <- tibble::tibble(
        scenario       = sname,
        parameter      = k,
        base_value     = format_h5_value(base_vals[[k]]),
        scenario_value = format_h5_value(scenario_vals[[k]])
      )
    }
  }
}
sheets$applied_settings <- dplyr::bind_rows(applied_rows) |>
  dplyr::arrange(parameter, scenario)
sheets <- c(sheets[c("base", "applied_settings")],
            sheets[param_grid$scenario_name])

xlsx_path <- file.path(tempdir(), "diagnose_green_roofs_params.xlsx")
writexl::write_xlsx(sheets, path = xlsx_path)
message("Wrote XLSX (", length(sheets), " sheets) to:\n  ", xlsx_path)
#> Wrote XLSX (11 sheets) to:
#>   C:\Users\RUNNER~1\AppData\Local\Temp\RtmpIP3jU8/diagnose_green_roofs_params.xlsx

What the verdicts decide

  • Check 2 FAIL → the growth curve is dead in this build — escalate to tandler.com (contradicts their answer 5 of 2026-10-08) before any production roof-type run. PASS with the “barely moves the total” note (the run-3 outcome) → the curve mechanics work, but the seasonal UrbanEVA factors barely influence the totals. The SWMM-UrbanEVA cross-check (2026-11-10, passed, see https://raindrop.kompetenz-wasser.io/optimisation/gruendach/urbaneva-gegencheck/) confirms the ET totals, and the decomposition puts transpiration at roughly 370 mm/a; what remains open is only why the seasonal growth modulation barely shapes the annual balance (query with tandler.com pending) and the engine-internal confirmation of the ET split.
  • Check 3 PASS → the production scenarios may give the roof its own curve (Growth_Dach) and e.g. keep the swale on separate grass factors, should Daniel supply any. FAIL → both elements share Growth_1 (the current default design: swale vegetation is seasonally similar anyway).
  • Check 4 STEP → monthly support points at month starts (what make_growth_curve() writes) are correct. LINEAR → switch the support points to month midpoints.
  • Check 1 failures stop the roof-type comparison until resolved with tandler.com — the applied-settings XLSX is the reproduction package.
